lessons.title: When programs break: exceptions and try-catch

objectives.cognitive: Distinguish a runtime exception from a compiler error and explain try-catch.
objectives.affective: Plan friendly recovery instead of letting a problem end the whole task.
objectives.psychomotor: Run and alter array and arithmetic exception examples.

blocks.markdown: Continue your Week 12 Vehicle family. This module upgrades those same classes; it does not create a different project theme. First verify each sample, then make Your task changes. Paper liplets are written and assessed separately. The personal performance-task project continues its own Week 12 theme.
An exception interrupts normal execution while a program runs. A compiler error prevents the program from running at all. A catch block handles a matching exception and decides what happens next.
A flat tire can end a jeepney trip. Preparing a spare tire is like a catch block: you plan a recovery so the trip can continue.

Reading example from printed Step 1: `for (int i = 0; i <= fleet.length; i++)` visits one slot too many. A three-vehicle array has indices 0, 1 and 2. The program prints those vehicles, then throws ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException at index 3; the final report line is skipped. Stack messages and line numbers vary by JVM. The required sample below corrects the condition so it can run successfully.

rows: Not required to catch or declare at compile time
The compiler requires catch or throws
Exception itself; FileNotFoundException in the printed real-file reference

blocks.markdown: Exception inherits from Throwable. RuntimeException inherits from Exception; its descendants are unchecked. A checked exception still needs a catch or throws declaration even if the risky situation never occurs during a particular run. Serious Error conditions are outside this lesson's recovery examples.

rows.means: A checked exception is neither caught nor declared.
rows.fix: Use a matching catch or declare throws X in the caller.

rows.see: Child is not abstract and does not override getCapacity()
rows.means: The new Vehicle contract is missing from a child.
rows.fix: Implement getCapacity in every concrete child.

rows.see: exception X has already been caught
rows.means: A broader catch appears before its specific child.
rows.fix: Put specific catches before general catches.

rows.see: InvalidDistanceException cannot be converted to Throwable
rows.means: The custom class is not an exception subclass.
rows.fix: Check extends Exception or extends RuntimeException.

performanceTask.title: Make your own Week 12 program crash-proof
performanceTask.markdown: Open your own Week 12 performance-task theme. Keep its parent and children and add exception handling. Include a checked custom exception, an unchecked custom exception, a throwing setter, safe Scanner input, multiple catches and finally. Test good input, letters, a negative value and a value that is too large. Explain what each catch does. The store example is a reference, not an instruction to replace your existing theme. Submit this version explicitly after testing; personal runs never complete module activities.
checklist: Continue your own Week 12 theme, not the Vehicle module
One checked and one unchecked custom exception, each using super(message)
A method declares and throws the checked exception
At least one try has two or more catch blocks
Catch messages are clear and friendly
Demonstrate good input, letters, negative values and too-large values; submit explicitly
presentationOutline: Introduce your theme and two custom exceptions (30 seconds)
Normal run with good input (1 minute)
Trigger each catch and custom exception safely (2 minutes)
Point to one checked and one unchecked exception and explain the choice (1 minute)
questionsToPrepare: What changes if try and catch are removed?
Why did you choose checked for one exception?
What prints when the try succeeds?
Where do throw and throws appear?
How does inheritance make your custom exception usable in a catch?
